verses.1: Oh, how beautiful are your garments! Oh, how magnificent are your decorations! Jerusalem is a holy city. Do not allow corruption and impurity to come into your midst again.
verses.2: I rise from my grave. My home is Jerusalem. I open my arms, and my beloved daughter is among them.
verses.3: For as Jehovah said, “You shall be sold and not redeemed with money.”
verses.4: For as the Lord God said, “My people have gone down into Egypt, and they will be there forever. And Assyria will destroy them in Epsos.”
verses.5: And now, what shall I do? Let the LORD be glorified, for my people have been taken captive by their rulers. May the LORD be glorified! And always, every day, my name will be remembered.
verses.6: Therefore, my people shall know that my name will be remembered on that day. I am indeed the one who will speak.
verses.7: May your feet rest on the mountains! May your steps bring peace and joy. May you bring salvation to Zion, O king of God.
verses.8: The voices of those who were near us united together, and they praised God together. For in their mutual gaze, they saw that Jehovah was indeed their Savior.
verses.9: May they together destroy the ruins of Jerusalem, so that Jehovah may comfort His people and save Jerusalem.
verses.10: The Lord has hidden His holy ones from the eyes of all nations. And all the people of the earth have seen our salvation.
verses.11: Let them go, let them leave that place. Do not touch them; let them get out of there. Let the servants of Jehovah be free from their troubles.
verses.12: For you shall not go out in haste, nor shall you go in a hurry. For the LORD is going before you, and the God of Israel is leading you along.
verses.13: Look, my servant Yarum will be raised up and brought to a higher place.
verses.14: As many of you have already heard, it’s like being covered with someone else’s hair; it’s something that humans can only imagine.
verses.15: So, many nations will fall upon him. Kings from all over will attack him, because he has not told them what they should do. They have seen nothing, and they have heard nothing; therefore, they will be destroyed.
